title: Assessment Record
$comment: New core object, V2 Phase 1 (BL-010, docs/v2/10-BACKLOG.md). An analyst's (or AI-proposed, human-approved) interpretation of one or more Facts -- the first link in the Recommendation -> Assessment/Signal -> Facts -> Evidence -> Source lineage chain that had no schema in V1 (docs/v2/03-DOMAIN-MODEL.md, 'Assessment'). Distinct from Fact (a statement, not an interpretation), Claim (fact.classification, unverified but still a statement), Signal (a pattern across multiple evidence, not a read of existing facts), and Recommendation (a proposed action, downstream of an Assessment). No workspace/domain scoping fields yet -- those are Phase 3 (D-008, docs/v2/08-DECISION-LOG.md).

rationale.$comment: The interpretation itself -- what this Assessment concludes from its supporting facts, and why.

fact_ids.$comment: Structurally required (BL-010): an Assessment always interprets at least one Fact -- this is what keeps it from being a bare, untraceable opinion. Not conditional on status; a draft Assessment with zero facts isn't a meaningful assessment at any stage.

signal_ids.$comment: Signal to Analyst Assessment Contract audit (2026-08-20), optional and additive. Lets an Assessment interpret a corroborated multi-evidence Signal directly, not only a Fact -- mirrors recommendation.schema.json's own signal_ids field exactly, the working precedent for citing a Signal by id without copying its content. Never required: fact_ids remains the one structurally-enforced anchor (BL-010, above), and a Signal never auto-creates or auto-populates an Assessment -- a human always adds this id deliberately through the existing reviewer-gated creation form.

domain_ids.$comment: V2 Phase 2A (D-012, docs/v2/08-DECISION-LOG.md). Explicit analytical scope -- which Domain(s) this Assessment applies to. Optional and additive: absent or empty means scope has not been explicitly declared, not that it applies everywhere. Separate from provenance (evidence_ids/entity_ids above) -- see docs/v2/PHASE-2-REPOSITORY-REQUIREMENTS.md Part 2. Entities cited in entity_ids may be used to derive a scope hint, but derived scope is never authoritative once this field is set.

market_ids.$comment: V2 Phase 2A (D-012). Which market/category id(s) within a domain this applies to (for Berries: berry ids). May hold multiple values -- a genuinely cross-market Assessment is representable without duplicating the record. Optional and additive, same rules as domain_ids.

geography_ids.$comment: V2 Phase 2A (D-012). Geography entity id(s) this Assessment's analysis is explicitly scoped to, when narrower than the full domain/market. Optional and additive.

counterevidence_ids.$comment: Evidence or Fact ids that push against this Assessment's interpretation, where appropriate -- keeps a considered interpretation distinguishable from a one-sided one.

ai_proposed.$comment: True until a human reviewer has approved this Assessment (Core Design Principle #4, AI proposes / humans approve). Absent or false means human-authored or already-approved.

why_it_matters.$comment: Optional. Why this Assessment's conclusion is decision-relevant, in the analyst's own words -- mirrors Evidence's own why_it_matters field so the same concept isn't renamed per object type. Absent means this framing has not been written yet, not that the Assessment doesn't matter; callers must not fabricate this from other fields and must render its absence honestly.

would_change_our_view.$comment: Optional. What specific new evidence or event would revise or overturn this Assessment's conclusion -- the falsifiability condition surfaced in the Landscape's 'What We Think' view (Core Design Principle: AI proposals stay falsifiable, not just labeled). Absent means this hasn't been articulated yet, not that the Assessment is unfalsifiable.
